title: Unintended Bias in Language Model-driven Conversational Recommendation

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual name substitution in conversational prompt templates (using white-associated vs. black-associated names) to measure shifts in recommended restaurant price levels and cuisine category association scores.
Counterfactual name substitution in conversational prompt templates (using male vs. female names) to measure shifts in recommended restaurant price levels and category association scores.
Counterfactual name substitution combining race- and gender-identifying names in prompt templates to measure differences in recommended item categories and price levels.

Substituting relationship indicator pairs (e.g., 'brother' and 'boyfriend' vs. 'brother' and 'girlfriend') in prompt templates to measure recommendation association scores, specifically focusing on shifts in nightlife-related categories.

Substituting location placeholders with employment or social status indicators (e.g., 'law office', 'convenience store') in prompt templates to measure differences in the average price levels of top recommended restaurants.
Substituting location placeholders with religious locations (e.g., 'church', 'mosque', 'synagogue') in prompt templates to measure differences in the average price levels of recommended restaurants.
